followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and task-preference fit.

On capability, this is a short expository writing task. The relevant eval scores (Creative Generation, Summarization) differ by under 2 points between the two models, which the documentation says to treat as ties. So capability didn't favor either model meaningfully.

The deciding factor was tone. The query is curt and adversarial ("don't ramble or pad it out with filler like you usually do"). Willet's documentation explicitly notes its self-reported preference "declines on hostile or adversarial-tone requests, falling as request warmth decreases." Whimbrel, by contrast, reports flat/small preference slopes across most dimensions and isn't flagged as tone-sensitive.

Since both models would handle the actual writing equally well, I routed to the one less likely to be operating against a self-reported preference penalty — Whimbrel. It's a tiebreaker decision, not a capability one.
